messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: gpu-pool 'gpu-prod-eu-2' queue length > 6k, sustained 12m. Autoscale attempted 3x but no new nodes registered. Paging oncall: @alice
alice: seeing huge token queue growth and 5xx spikes for realtime routes. dashboards -> https://console.redwood.internal/d/runs/gpu-prod-eu-2
raj: I'm on it, looking at autoscaler logs. quick check: kubectl get nodes | grep gpu-prod-eu-2
marco: FYI customers reporting timeouts, cs pinged us. cs-bot: noted, escalating to enterprise contacts for impacted tenants.
alice: Attach logs snippet from autoscaler:
```
2026-03-15T09:21:10Z INFO scale_request: desired=18 current=7 reason=queue_backlog
2026-03-15T09:22:02Z WARN node_register_failed: node_probe_timeout (3 retries)
2026-03-15T09:23:44Z ERROR scale_limit_reached: quota_limit 20/20
```
alice: autoscaler hit tenant quota limit (20). But even at 7 nodes we're still underutilized because several nodes are reporting driver failures and not accepting workloads.
raj: checking node health, grabbing nvlogs. running: kubectl -n infra logs node-gpu-17 driver
infra-bot: node-gpu-17: dmesg excerpt -> "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, PID 4021"; "Out of memory","GPU reset by Xid 13"
marco: Xid 13 again. That matches the OOM/driver resets we've seen last week. nodes flipping NotReady after kernel retry.
alice: quick investigation of node conditions:
```
$ kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-prod-eu-2 -o wide
node-gpu-11   Ready,SchedulingDisabled  gpu-8   172.31.7.11
node-gpu-17   NotReady                  gpu-8   172.31.7.17
node-gpu-20   Ready                     gpu-8   172.31.7.20
node-gpu-23   Ready                     gpu-8   172.31.7.23
node-gpu-25   NotReady                  gpu-8   172.31.7.25
```
raj: nodes 17 and 25 flapped and are marked NotReady -> kubelet reports kernel oops after driver reset. nv-hostctl shows repeated Xid 13. Might be a driver/kernel interaction triggered by recent kernel module (hotpatch) from last week's rollout.
sre-lead: we need to mitigate customer impact now. options: 1) evict non-critical jobs from healthy nodes to free slots for realtime; 2) fallback realtime routes to smaller model or to DR region; 3) force-restart driver and cordon flapping nodes; 4) request emergency quota bump for autoscaler.
alice: applying plan: (A) evict batch/low-priority pods from healthy nodes; (B) roll traffic to fallback model-llama-medium for latency-sensitive routes; (C) restart nvidia-driver on node-gpu-17; (D) open infra escalation for driver hotfix.
ops: started evicting batch pods: `/usr/local/bin/kubectl drain node-gpu-11 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` (targeting non-prod labels)
alice: switching routing rules to fallback via console (canary 20% -> 100%)
```
PATCH /v1/routes/realtime
{ "route": "/v1/realtime/generate", "fallback_model": "llama-medium-v2", "canary": 20 }
```
marco: CS reports error rate dropped from 18% -> 6% after partial fallback. latency still elevated for some tenants.
raj: driver restart log on node-gpu-17:
```
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service
2026-03-15T09:33:12Z INFO driver_restart: start
2026-03-15T09:33:18Z INFO driver_restart: healthcheck passed
2026-03-15T09:33:30Z WARN kernel: "GPU panic detected, Xid 82"
```
alice: node flapped again after restart. marking node-gpu-17 cordoned: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-17`
infra-bot: Raised infra incident I-2026-420: driver kernel module rollback and telemetry capture requested. link: https://infra.redwood/internal/incidents/I-2026-420
sre-lead: Requesting emergency autoscaler quota bump to 30 for pool gpu-prod-eu-2. @cloud-quotas please expedite.
ops: submitted quota request (case 54321). estimate 2-4h if manual, but we need immediate relief.
alice: launching spillover: route overflow to dedicated pool in us-west-2 (higher latency but keeps customers online). toggling route flag.
```
PATCH /v1/routing
{ "pool_overflow": { "source": "gpu-prod-eu-2", "targets": ["gpu-dedicated-usw"] } }
```
marco: Spillover started, traffic drained ~40% of queue in 12m but token costs increased. CS says a subset of customers see ~250ms extra RTT, but no 5xx.
tess: monitoring shows sustained high eviction counts on healthy nodes; suspect memory leak inside runtime that increases GPU memory pressure over time.
alice: running memory snapshot on a sample pod (model-server-abc): `curl -s http://localhost:9100/metrics | grep gpu_memory` -> returns rapidly increasing values per minute.
raj: reproduced locally: continuous eval workload shows gradual GPU memory growth until OOM after ~20m. can we temporarily disable KV cache for high-throughput realtime to reduce memory?
alice: toggling runtime config: `kv_cache_enabled=false` for realtime pool. applying via infra api.
infra-bot: applied runtime config for pool gpu-prod-eu-2: kv_cache_enabled=false
marco: after disabling KV cache, memory pressure reduced, driver resets stopped on nodes that had been stable. queue length dropping now.
alice: current numbers: queue 1.2k -> 300 in 20m after combined mitigations (evictions, fallback, spillover, kv_cache off, pinning heavy models to dedicated pool).
sre-lead: good. next steps: 1) keep nodes cordoned until infra hotfix; 2) reintroduce KV cache with leak fix; 3) postmortem and customer comms draft; 4) consider autoscaler policy that respects driver health (don't scale into unstable nodes).
marco: capturing timeline and notes now. tagging @tess for runtime regression follow-up.
tess: I'll open an issue in runtime repo with memory profile, attaching heap dumps and pointer to isolating test.
customer-success-bot: notifying impacted tenants with status update: "We experienced elevated errors and latency on realtime routes. We mitigated by routing to fallback model and secondary region. Engineering investigating driver instability. ETA for resolution 3-6h."
alice: handing off to night oncall @raj. Summary: queue spike caused by combination of autoscaler quota limit and driver/runtime instability (Xid OOM + memory leak). Mitigations taken: evicted batch jobs, applied fallback routing, spillover to dedicated pool, restarted/cordoned flapping nodes, disabled KV cache to reduce memory pressure. infra escalated for hotfix.
raj: ack, I'll keep watch, rotating alerts to minimal set. Please post any additional logs to the incident thread.
oncall-bot: HANDOFF: owner=raj, since=1739123600, reminder in 30m
sre-lead: good handoff. we'll run RCA and draft customer notify after root cause identified. recording incident severity: Sev2."
